author: Valerie Anne
title: You Oughta Know That Alanis Morissette Is Pansexual
content:
feature image photo by Credit: NBC / Contributor via Getty Images

It’s official: 90s icon and present-day superstar Alanis Morissette is pansexual. The singer was a guest on the Handsome podcast, which is co-hosted by queer comedians Tig Notaro, Fortune Feimster, and Mae Martin, and they were talking about Alanis’s penchant for a post-breakup rage anthem. Fortune Feimster jokingly asked her, “Did it make you want to be a lesbian at any point?” to which Alanis replied, “I’m pansexual, so yeah.”

The energy in the room was perfect. At first, everyone thought it was a joke (or perhaps that she was being…ironic), but when they clarified that Alanis was serious, they all joked that she should have led with that. You walk into a queer podcast with the queer announcement!!

Granted, this is not the first time Alanis has said she isn’t straight. She has been talking about exploring her sexuality and being attracted to women as far back as 2008, and it was apparently at least partly her idea for her character to kiss Sarah Jessica Parker’s Carrie during her Sex and the City guest spot. It’s just the first time she’s used a specific label out loud.

I considered riddling this intro with Alanis-related puns (like the joke my friend made: she’s got one pan in her pocket…) but I’ll save you the cringe. I’ll just say this news has made me even more head over feet for her.

author: Valerie Anne
title: ‘Criminal Minds’ Has Unceremoniously Been Canceled
content:
In devastating news for me specifically, it was announced that the upcoming 20th season of Criminal Minds will be its last. What’s worse is that they had already finished filming the series by the time this news broke, and this abrupt cancellation means we won’t even get a proper series finale, even though there will have been over 370 episodes by the time the new season finishes airing. It feels like a slap in the face this show doesn’t deserve!

Now, there’s always the chance another network saves them from oblivion; it’s happened once before. The first 15 seasons of the show aired on CBS from 2005-2020, but then two years later it was revived as Criminal Minds: Evolution on Paramount+ without much structural change. We still had most of the same characters, only now they could say “fuck”, which they did with much aplomb. It is also in this Evolution series that Nicole Pacent joined the show as Rebecca Wilson, who became a love interest for long-standing member of the BAU family Tara Lewis, played by Aisha Tyler.

The shortening from 22 episodes to 10 was a hard one to bear, but I was grateful for anything after that two-year dark period. The bonus gayness didn’t hurt. Unfortunately, this did lead to some disappointing side effects, like the fact that Tara and Rebecca got married entirely off-screen between seasons. author: Audrey Black
title: Dallas Gayborhood Fights Back Against Removal of Rainbow Crosswalks
content:
For years, rainbow crosswalks marked each end of Cedar Springs Road, the iconic strip in Oak Lawn, Dallas’s beloved gayborhood.

As a native Texan, I vividly remember the first time I saw Oak Lawn’s rainbow crosswalks. I was excited to see such a visible sign of belonging and it led me to learn more about Dallas’ rich LGBTQ+ history. I immediately felt welcome and spent more and more time in Oak Lawn as the years passed.

“[The crosswalks] meant inclusion, acceptance, diversity,” David Fisher, an Oak Lawn resident and election judge at the Oak Lawn Branch Library, told me. They communicated that, “this is a neighborhood that’s accepting, and people should feel … comfortable, and like they belong.”

“They almost served as a demarcation point of the Cedar Springs corridor, the neighborhood, of like, ‘This is our street,’” Lee Daugherty, owner of the long-standing gay bar Alexandre’s on Cedar Springs and an active member of the Cedar Springs Merchant Association, told me. “We have long historical ties and cultural ties to this area and to the street. It was a recognition of those who came before, the work they did, the struggle they had, and the continued struggle we have going forward.”

“Symbolically it was … a welcome mat: You are welcome here. Everyone is welcome here,” Daughtery continued. “A lot of people I’ve talked to who are much younger than me, or got here during their teenage years or early adulthood, felt it was the first time they saw a physical representation of being welcome and being home.”

In October 2025, Governor Greg Abbott directed state transportation officials to enforce rules against certain roadway markings, threatening to withhold transportation funding from cities that failed to comply. Officials cited concerns about driver distraction, even though the rainbow crosswalks had been in place for years and similar markings were allowed to remain. Dallas’s Oak Lawn rainbows were slated for removal.

This follows the directive of the Trump administration, who has argued for uniform street markings nationwide as a “safety initiative.” This transparent act of censorship has forced multiple cities in Texas and Florida to remove their crosswalks.

Many studies have found that decorative crosswalks actually make drivers more attentive. The Knight Creative Communities Institute found drivers drove roughly 25% slower around the decorative crosswalks installed near schools. Bloomberg Philanthropy found a 50% decrease in the rate of crashes involving pedestrians around decorated crosswalks. Yet despite this evidence, these street markings are being censored.

The crosswalks in Dallas had faced scrutiny before. The community had already paid to refurbish them in an effort to meet roadway requirements, replacing solid blocks of color with a striped design. That investment did not spare them from removal.

When it became obvious that crosswalks might be a target, the Cedar Springs Merchants Association, composed of bar and shop owners along Cedar Springs, raised funds along with the LGBTQ Chamber to paint their crosswalks in compliance with standards, Susie Hess explained to me. Hess is a Dallas County Democratic Party precinct chair and former president of Stonewall Democrats of Dallas, a political organization representing the interests of LGBTQ community in the Dallas area. “The only difference was instead of white stripes, they used colors,” Hess explained. “Governor Abbott’s decision to pressure cities into removing these was just petty and really targeted.”

“It took years to get these things installed,” Daughtery said. “Then they were installed and weren’t installed correctly. We had to go back and spend even more years, and then we finally got them removed and put down the right way.”

The rainbow crossings were not the only community-funded symbols targeted. South Dallas’s “All Black Lives Matter” crossings, first dedicated on Martin Luther King Jr. Day in 2022, were targeted under the same directive. Crews removed them in March 2026. The state’s official stated concern was roadway safety and distraction. Meanwhile, the Southern Methodist University mascot, the red Mustang, remained embedded in the intersection of Hillcrest Road and Daniel Avenue in University Park. Officials said they considered the intersection compliant with the directive and that the Texas Department of Transportation had requested no further action.

As Hess put it: “It’s okay to have pride in your school, but not pride in who you are?”.

“They’re threatened by our vibrant, wonderful, accepting community where people can just be who they are,” Hess added.

After months of uncertainty and an unsuccessful request for an exception, Dallas began removing the crossings in March 2026. The actual removal came without warning for community members.

“We were planning a neat photo where everyone would come out and take one last photo, something for the history books,” Daugherty said. “That never happened.”

After hearing about the state directive, Rev. Rachel Griffin-Allison, senior pastor of Oak Lawn United Methodist Church, proposed painting the church’s front steps at the corner of Oak Lawn Avenue and Cedar Springs Road. One of the church’s security guards, who also worked as a painter, helped turn the staircase into a Progress Pride flag.

author: Valerie Anne
title: ‘The Hunting Wives’ Season 2 Trailer Has Sapphic Sex and Sad Exes
content:
Season one of The Hunting Wives was a wild ride, and I have a feeling season two is going to be even wilder. The full trailer dropped and it has me clapping and kicking my feet at the sapphic chaos about to descend upon us.

The trailer opens with Sophie’s husband asking if Sophie is “still dreaming about her” (“her” being Margo) and a few flashing scenes implies that yes, yes she is.

Other things we see flash by: a glam cowgirl photo shoot, Margo being manipulative to all kinds of people, and Callie being a sad ex and using a photo of Margo as target practice.

This show also knows exactly what it is and is leaning into it. For example, the song playing is Nancy Sinatra’s “Bang Bang”, which is the perfect backdrop for this trailer full of guns and sex and chaos. And the tagline for the season is “someone is going down,” which the narrator says while the visuals cut between a dead body and also a more…explicit interpretation of the phrase.

Based on how season one ended, I can’t wait to find out how Sophie ends up back in Margo’s bed (and her bubble bath!), and luckily we only have one month left to wait.

title: ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Kicked Off Season 23 With a Sapphic Smooch
content:
Grey’s Anatomy came back with a bang. (Well, a smooch. But we’ll get there.) Amelia spent the entire episode getting the cold shoulder from Toni because, as I’m sure you remember, we left them last season with Toni showing up at Amelia’s door to profess her love for her, only to realize a naked Cass was already in Amelia’s apartment.

When we return for season 23(!), Toni is giving Amelia the cold shoulder all day. Amelia desperately wants to talk to her, but Toni isn’t hearing her out. They clash over work decisions, and Amelia starts to get frustrated. And at this point I was afraid the show was ending their storyline. I thought it was going to be a dramatic fight and then back to no wlw relationships on the show. I was thankfully wrong!

Eventually, the day leads Amelia to Toni’s front door, where she apologizes again for sleeping with Cass, and explains it was an emotional reaction to being so sure Toni was about get back together with her ex. She regrets it if it means she would lose Toni. She says she’s truly, madly, deeply in love with Toni and that if Toni is done, she’ll move on, but if not, she really doesn’t want to let what they have died. Toni considers her for a moment but then breaks; she’s still in love with Amelia, and she’s not done. author: Valerie Anne
title: ‘The Body’ Is a Sapphic, Ritual-Gone-Wrong Teen Horror Show Coming to Netflix
content:
Do you ever feel like a show was made just for you using all your favorite media keywords? That’s how I felt when I first heard about Netflix’s The Body. I saw Catholic school, dancers, ritual-gone-wrong, horror and I was beyond sold.

And in case those words and phrases didn’t make it obvious: The story is also sapphic. Writer and creator Quinn Shephard (who acted in movies like The Miseducation of Cameron Post and wrote/directed episodes of Under the Bridge) started writing the show the year she came out. She says: “It’s satirizing some of the trauma of growing up queer and repressed and the confusion around that.”

A lot of the main cast of girls are relative newcomers on the scene (aka they don’t have Wikipedia “personal life” pages yet) so I’m not sure who among them are queer, but the show WILL feature lesbian reality star Gabby Windey in a recurring role as a coach. Also, almost all of the episodes have women listed as writers.

The show looks freaky and weird in all the best ways, and I can’t wait. I hope it’s just as fun as shows like Yellowjackets and even Mike Flanagan’s Carrie. May the teens-getting-into-supernatural-mischief genre never die.

The series drops next month and you can watch the full official trailer right now!
